title: Legacy audit event migration: dual-write legacy + schema-v1 event names, then cutover
creator: Mei Lin
description:
We are standardizing audit logs to the canonical schema v1. Several services (gateway, console backend, rbac, deployment controllers, exporter) currently emit legacy event names and/or legacy payload shapes.

This ticket covers the migration strategy to avoid breaking enterprise exports and existing internal queries:
- Dual-write: emit both (a) schema-v1 event_name + payload and (b) legacy event_name variant for an agreed deprecation window.
- Cutover: per-environment flag to stop emitting legacy names once (1) customers are notified, (2) dashboards/coverage scanner confirm parity, and (3) exporters/consumers confirm compatibility.
- Deprecation warnings + change notes: add warnings in docs and customer-facing release notes for any event_name changes.

Why this matters:
- Enterprise customers often pin SIEM searches/detections to specific event names. We need a stable window to update detections.
- Internally, Security/GRC needs continuity in evidence exports while moving to schema-v1 canonical fields.

Scope
In-scope:
- Define mapping table: legacy_event_name -> schema_v1.event_name (and any field transforms/renames).
- Implement dual-write in services that still emit legacy names.
- Add feature flags / config knobs:
  - AUDIT_LOG_DUAL_WRITE_LEGACY=true|false
  - AUDIT_LOG_LEGACY_WRITE_CUTOFF_DATE (optional soft guard; log error if legacy is still enabled past date)
- Add a deprecation plan + customer change notes template.
- Ensure exporters don’t duplicate downstream delivery when dual-writing (avoid double-counting or duplicate exports).

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Full historical backfill for legacy logs.
- Customer-specific custom formats.

Implementation plan
1) Identify the event_name set requiring migration
- Use sensitive action inventory + coverage scanner output to list all audited actions and confirm which currently produce legacy names.
- Focus first on enterprise-visible actions: API keys, RBAC policy changes, user/admin management, org/workspace settings, model rollout actions, dedicated scaling, private installer events.

2) Finalize mapping + backwards-compat rules
- Create a canonical mapping list (shared in Confluence + in-repo as a checked-in file used by tooling).
- Rules:
  - schema_v1.event_name is canonical; legacy_event_name is emitted as an additional event only during deprecation.
  - schema_v1.schema_version stays stable ("1.0") even during dual-write.
  - When legacy payload has fields that violate redaction policy, legacy variant must be the redacted equivalent (no secrets/tokens), even if older logs historically included more data.

3) Dual-write implementation
- Add shared helper in audit library to emit canonical + legacy alias in one call to minimize drift.
- Ensure both variants share:
  - request_id / trace_id
  - actor + org context
  - outcome + error semantics
  - stable timestamp ordering (best-effort) to avoid confusing downstream.

4) Prevent double-counting
- Exporter: dedupe strategy must not collapse distinct event_names incorrectly.
- Metrics: maintain separate counters for canonical vs legacy emission:
  - auditlog_emitted_total{event_name=...}
  - auditlog_emitted_total{event_name=..., variant="legacy_alias"}

5) Cutover
- Stage first: enable dual-write in staging for 1 week; confirm parity of counts by event category (allowing for minor timing differences).
- Production: enable dual-write for beta customers first (via org allowlist) if supported; otherwise enable globally but keep legacy in place.
- Set cutover date (target: 30 days after GA, unless customer contracts require longer).
- Remove legacy names after cutoff and keep the mapping file for historical reference.

Acceptance criteria
- Mapping table exists and is reviewed by Security Eng (Marcus Lin / delegate) + GRC (Olga Petrov delegate) and published/linked from audit logging program docs.
- For each migrated action, we can demonstrate in staging:
  - canonical schema-v1 event is emitted and validates
  - legacy alias event is emitted during dual-write window
  - both have the same request_id and actor attribution
- Exporter does not regress (no repeated retries due to payload changes; no duplicate sink writes beyond expected dual-write semantics).
- Customer-facing change notes prepared (event rename list + how to update SIEM queries).

Risks / open questions
- Some customers may treat duplicate events (dual-write) as alerts if they query on action occurrence rather than event_name. We should explicitly communicate that dual-write will generate two records per action and recommend filtering by schema_v1.event_name.
- Need to confirm whether any internal detections in Splunk are keyed off legacy names and update them before cutover.

comments: 2025-05-29 — Mei Lin (creator): Creating this ticket to centralize migration work. We keep finding one-off legacy names in gateway/rbac/controllers. Need a single mapping + deprecation plan so we can answer enterprise questionnaires consistently.

2025-06-03 — Benji Okafor (assignee): Drafted initial mapping list from code search. Biggest offenders: rbac.role.* legacy names and console admin actions. Will circulate mapping for review once Kaitlyn/Amara confirm the exact code paths.

2025-06-07 — Marcus Lin: Please ensure legacy variants ALSO run through the same redaction rules as canonical. Don’t preserve legacy payloads “as-is” if they included sensitive keys. Add test coverage for common secret-ish keys (token, api_key, secret, authorization, cookie).

2025-06-10 — Nadia Rahman: From pipeline perspective, dual-write is fine but we need metrics tagged by variant to keep SLO and drop-rate clean. Also, please don’t attempt sampling for legacy (audit logs must be complete).

2025-06-13 — Naomi Feldman: Customer-facing notes need to be explicit: which event names change, recommended query updates, deprecation timeline. Sales/SE will want a one-pager they can paste into security review follow-ups.

2025-06-18 — Benji Okafor: Implemented helper API sketch in shared library: emitCanonicalWithLegacyAlias(canonicalName, legacyName, payload). Next step is wiring into gateway + rbac bundle service. Will post PR once tests are green.

2025-06-21 — Sahana Iyer: Suggest CI check: if a legacy event name exists in mapping, ensure it’s not used directly anywhere except via the dual-write helper. This prevents drift where teams add new legacy emissions by mistake.
